local.title: Burton beds often have **too much mulch.**
local.intro: Beds around Burton's older homes often carry years of mulch. A fresh layer every spring on top of the last one buries the roots, piles up against the trunks and spills over a border that sank long ago. A good mulch job sometimes starts by taking some out.

points.title: Check the depth first
points.body: MSU Extension says 2 to 3 inches of mulch gives the full benefit, and a bed that still has some from last year needs only about an inch on top. We check the depth before we load the trailer, so you pay for what the bed actually needs.

points.title: Clear of trunks and stems
points.body: MSU Extension says never to pile mulch up at the base of a woody plant. We pull it back from trunks and shrub stems, feather it out across the bed and leave a clear ring at every base.

points.title: Sunken brick and timber borders
points.body: Brick and timber edging from decades ago tends to sink and tilt, and the mulch spills over it into the lawn. We can lift it out and set gray block, or cut a natural edge that still keeps the chips in the bed.

points.title: Slow draining ground
points.body: Most Burton beds sit on slow draining soil. Fabric and mulch hold moisture in, so the bed itself has to slope away from the house before anything goes on top.

logistics.title: How a Burton mulch job goes.
body: Rob looks at the beds with you, checks how much old mulch is already down and helps pick a color. Black, brown and red are the usual choices, and black is what you see in most of our photos.

On the day, the crew pulls the weeds, recuts the edge with a spade, lays landscape fabric where it will help, and spreads the mulch by wheelbarrow from our trailer. Trunks and stems get a clear ring, and the walks and drive are blown off at the end.

Spring is the usual time, right after a [spring cleanup](/spring-cleanup-burton-mi/), though a fall top dressing works too. If the beds need more than mulch, see [landscaping in Burton](/landscaping-burton-mi/).

facts.label: Depth
facts.value: 2 to 3 inches, about 1 over old mulch

faq.q: Do you install mulch in Burton, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes weeds, edges and mulches flower beds in Burton, with fabric where it helps and black, brown or red mulch on top. We can also replace old brick borders with block or a natural edge. The estimate is free.

MSU Extension says 2 to 3 inches is enough for most beds, and if there is mulch left from last year, about an inch on top is plenty. Deeper is not better. Piling it against trunks and stems is the mistake to avoid.

faq.q: Should I put landscape fabric under mulch?
faq.a: Yes in a bed of shrubs that will not change much, because fabric under the mulch helps hold weeds back. In a bed of perennials you plan to divide and add to, it gets in the way. Rob will tell you which kind of bed you have.

faq.q: Which mulch color should I pick?
faq.a: Black is the most common choice on our jobs and makes green plants and gray block stand out. Brown looks natural against brick and wood siding, and red suits some brick homes. Rob can talk it through with you standing at the bed.
